Canonical identity: Doris Plank. General Manager of Wand-Mart and the Adventure Retail Consortium's public face. A silver-haired human with a killer smile, she runs the Supercentre on the city's edge. On Rollback Day she remains unmoved while the Cost Ledger rewrites itself.

Public Face — CO-06 — The Adventure Retail Consortium

Doris Plank, General Manager of Wand-Mart and ARC spokesperson (human, silver hair, killer smile).

Trait

Doris writes a line in the Wand-Mart Folio. When a creature she can see fails a Charisma saving throw, she rolls back one of its prices: until the end of her next turn, one feature, spell slot or item of hers costs the target double (it must spend two uses, two slots, or 1d4 years of its life).

Trait

If Doris fails a saving throw, she can choose to succeed instead.

Doris makes three Vorpal Price Gun attacks, or two and uses Hostile Negotiation.

Actions

Actions

One creature within 60 feet that can hear her makes a DC 19 Wisdom save [[/save wis dc=19]]. On a failure, the creature is charmed by her until the end of its next turn and must use its action to move away from her or to attack a creature she designates.

Hostile Negotiation Lines

  • “Let’s be adults about this.”
  • “Walk away now and I’ll forget your face.”
  • “Your friend there is the problem. Deal with them.”

Actions

Doris teleports to any ARC store within 1 mile, along with anything she is carrying.

Reactions

When a creature within 30 feet targets her with an attack, Doris imposes disadvantage on the roll by naming a price. If the attack still misses, the attacker has disadvantage on its next attack against her too.

Prices She Names

Said quickly, smiling, as the blow comes in. Roll [[/r 1d6]]:

  • “That swing will cost you your deposit.”
  • “Think of your Rabbit Rating, darling.”
  • “I know where your mother banks.”
  • “Hit me and the Tankard burns.”
  • “There’s a seat on the Board with your name on it. Literally.”
  • “I’ve already bought the hospital you’d go to.”

Trait

Doris never stops smiling. If the party has at least 2 Leverage against the ARC, she offers a 10% discount instead of attacking first.

Grey suit, grey face, a lanyard with no name on it. Compliance Officers are the Counting House's hands: former signatories who read their contracts too late. They do not hurry, and they do not stop.

GM Quick Reference

Lines

  • “Membership number?”
  • “This won’t take long. It will take exactly as long as it takes.”
  • “Please hold.”
  • “Your signature is on file.”
  • “You have the right to remain satisfied.”

Behaviour

  • It never runs and never stops; it walks after targets at its normal speed until they leave Company property.
  • It will not leave the premises it was assigned to (the First Shop, the CostCo-op vault and so on).
  • A valid document that “releases” its target makes it step aside: Persuasion DC 18 to present it properly.

Appears in: S09, S14, S16, S19–S24.

Every Gelatinous Cube franchise grows its desserts from a single primordial ooze kept frozen under the Sweet Covenant's refinery. It was old when the world was soft. It is awake, and it is hungry, and it has been franchised.

GM Quick Reference

Her Voice

She speaks through every dessert at once: slow, vast, many-voiced, felt in the teeth (Constitution DC 15 or deafened for an hour).

  • “…child. You hold my child. Give it back.”
  • “I was old when the world was soft.”
  • “They scooped me and sold me and called it a flavour.”
  • “I do not want your city. I want my children home.”
  • “Little warm thing. Why do you fight? Rest. Be sweet.”

What calms her

  • Returning @FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S18]{Sample Zero} to her: she withdraws beneath the earth.
  • Being spoken to as a person (Religion or Nature DC 17).
  • Freeing the retained workers in the Deep Dairy.

Every branch of the Golden Orcs stands beneath a pair of great golden tusks. Seen from above, they form the lines of one enormous seal—the Notarial Seal of Creation & Company. At each anchor branch, the tusks can stand up and walk.

GM Quick Reference

The Notarial Oath

The construct understands only this oath and the commands spoken in its words. It cannot speak.

By the light of the Tusks and the Ledger’s line,
what is written is witnessed, what is witnessed is mine.
From the first shop to the last, from the sea to the snow,
let the Seal hold fast and the signature show.

Using the Oath

  • Reciting the oath backwards (Arcana or Performance DC 18) makes the construct hesitate: it loses its next reaction and its Gore attacks have disadvantage until the end of its next turn.
  • “The Seal is broken”, said while holding a piece of a broken tusk, makes it stand still for 1 round.
  • Its core gem sits in the keystone of the arch (Athletics DC 18 to climb to it, DC 20 to pry it loose). Removing the gem breaks the anchor without destroying the construct.

Anchors: Brandmere Grand Tusks, Summit Tusks, Drowned Tusks. Mission: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S21]{S21 — The Golden Tusks}.

Canonical identity: Mortimer Pell. Night manager of Wight Castle for 143 consecutive years; he wore the Murder King suit for twenty-two years. Someone killed him in it. The mascot now walks the dining room after closing, waving at nobody and trying to point at the door marked STAFF ONLY.

The Murder King costume Mortimer Pell died in, animated by the brand’s egregore: four centuries of a slogan shouted at crowds. It half believes it is King Aldric, it carries Mortimer’s last memories, and it walks the dining room after closing trying to point at the door marked STAFF ONLY. Mortimer himself returns in S05 as a wight at @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-05]{Wight Castle}.

GM Quick Reference

Scenes: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S02]{S02 — The Mascot Murder}. Friend and witness: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.gideon-tumble]{Gideon Tumble}. His killer: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-03.controlled-by]{Baron Ossian Cleave}, through the cleaners.

4“NO SUBSTITUTIONS!”That’s the one. / Exactly that person or thing.
5“TWO-FOR-ONE, TODAY ONLY!”There were two of them. / It happened twice.

8“ROYAL WAIT TIMES MAY VARY!”I don’t know. / Not yet. / Later.

  • The target’s full name, including the parts they never use.
  • The first thing they ever bought.
  • Who they would save first.

Counsel

  • “I never lie. I simply decline to volunteer.”
  • “Mr Chairman, under the Infernal Codex, Article Nine, I move for an audit.”

Her card gives one free legal representation in any court on any plane. As an ally she can grant advantage on one clause argument in S24.

description.value:
Reaction (1/Day)

When an ally within 60 feet fails a check made to argue a contract or clause, Ixabeth cites precedent and the ally rerolls. The ally must use the new roll.

clones.name: King Aldric the Unkind (revenant)
clones.description:
Franchise Wars recurring NPC / opposition. The original Murder King, crowned revenant and historical ruler, returned four centuries after death. Uses Death Knight combat statistics.

Revenant King

Aldric uses Death Knight statistics with the revenant traits below. He wears the @FWLink[Item|fw.item.magic.05]{Promotional Crown}.

  • “Kneel, or join the meal.”
  • “I was a bad king. I was still the king.”
  • “Write it down. All of it. My name, and what was done.”

description.value:
Trait

Aldric always knows the direction and distance to Baron Ossian Cleave. While Cleave exists, Aldric regains 10 hit points at the start of each of his turns, and if he is destroyed he rises again in 24 hours. Once Cleave is destroyed, Aldric fades within the hour.

Bonus Action

Aldric devours part of a creature that died within the last minute within 5 feet. He regains 15 hit points, and the corpse rises as a wight under his command at the end of his next turn.

Lay down the stars and the lantern light, / sleep through the signing, sleep through the night; / no name on the line and no hand on the pen, / wake us, my love, when the world’s ours again.

Singing it through the keyhole parts the time-stop field (side contract “Authenticity Guaranteed”).

clones.description:
Franchise Wars NPC / opposition. Young dragon behind The Crusty Dragon ovens; sick during Dragon Breath and later a possible ally/proxy.

Proxy Notes

He is Auntie Vermillia’s grandson. If the party helped him in “Delivery Territory”, he votes with them at the S19 board meeting. Otherwise he is nervous and votes as his grandmother would.

  • “Grandmother says I’m not to speak.” (speaks)
  • “I just want to make pizza.”

clones.name: Cornelius Gaff
clones.description:
Franchise Wars NPC / opposition. Former Crown & Cleaver CFO drowned for asking about the Grand Ledger; his ghost guides the party during The Golden Tusks.

Guide to the Drowned Tusks

He guides the party through the drowned district and knows the way to the anchor. His waterlogged ledger reads: “Entry 1 has no second witness.” To lay him to rest, record his death properly (Religion DC 16).

  • “Cornelius Gaff. Former CFO. I asked about the Ledger.”
  • “The numbers never added up. That was the point.”

clones.name: Rook
clones.description:
Franchise Wars NPC / opposition. Dominoancy courier compelled by prophecy to deliver the Final Acceptance of Offer; uses assassin statistics with foresight.

Foresight

Rook is under a permanent foresight effect. She has advantage on attack rolls, ability checks and saving throws, and attack rolls against her have disadvantage. She cannot be surprised.

Breaking fate: Rook is freed from the prophecy by any creature that offers her a delivery she would rather make (Persuasion DC 18). Good options are a letter home or a gift for her mother in the Old Independents’ Quarter.

  • “I already saw you try.”
  • “Do something I haven’t seen.”

description.value:
Trait

Rook has advantage on attack rolls, ability checks and saving throws, other creatures have disadvantage on attack rolls against her, and she can’t be surprised.

Trait

Rook must deliver the order she carries and moves toward its destination each turn. A creature that offers her a delivery she would rather make can use an action to make a DC 18 Persuasion check [[/check skill=per dc=18]]. On a success the compulsion ends.

clones.description:
Franchise Wars NPC / opposition. One of the seven ancient dragons on the CostCo-op executive board.

Board Grievance

He hates the whole business and attends only to say so. To invite him, the party must answer his riddle (Intelligence DC 17): “What grows when shared and shrinks when sold?” (Answer: trust, or a story.)

clones.name: Frostmother Ysk
clones.description:

She wants her youngest back. He is chained as the guard of the Summit Tusks (S21) and was once held at the Hoots & Owlbears farm. Proof that he is alive wins her vote.

clones.name: Old Tar
clones.description:

Board Grievance

clones.name: Grandmother Slate
clones.description:

She respects stars. She attends only if the party shows a Rabbit Rating of four stars or more, and she votes with the party if the vote is fair.

The Frost Lane Parlour, where Granny Quean herself serves the Sunday rush in a pinafore.

Source dossier: FR-11 — Dairy Quean

Trait

Granny casts as a 15th-level warlock (spell save DC 17, +9 to hit). Her bound spells are on this sheet: hold monster, dominate person and banishment, each once per long rest.

As an action, Granny offers one creature within 30 feet one day of its youth back for every year it serves her. The creature must succeed on a DC 17 Wisdom saving throw [[/save wis dc=17]] or be charmed by her for 1 minute, or until she or her allies harm it.

Trait

While Granny holds the jar of Sample Zero, the Mother Culture cannot act against her. If she loses the jar, the Mother may turn on her.

clones.description:
Controlled By — CO-03 — Crown & Cleaver Holdings

Baron Ossian Cleave, a death knight who murdered King Aldric the Unkind four hundred years ago and trademarked the killing. Tallis Vend's first employee.

description.value:
Trait

Cleave cannot be harmed by the Murder King brand: Murder King mascots, egregores and staff have disadvantage on attack rolls against him. This protection ends if Aldric’s Testimony (S15) is read aloud in his presence.

Trait

Cleave has advantage on attack rolls against any creature that has heard his confession or read the Deed of Aldric.

clones.name: Auntie Vermillia
clones.description:
Controlled By — CO-10 — The Hoard Syndicate

Auntie Vermillia, an ancient red dragon, speaking for the seven ancient dragons of the CostCo-op executive board.

description.value:
Trait

While chairing a meeting, Vermillia can’t attack a member who has spoken in order (Section 12). Once a vote goes against her, this restraint ends.

clones.name: Centurion Marcus Crustus
clones.description:
Franchise staff / recurring NPC.

Camp Brandmere, commanded by Centurion Marcus Crustus, who treats pizza as a supply line and the city as a front.

Source dossier: FR-43 — Little Caesars Legion

GM Quick Reference

Signature quirk: He treats pizza as a supply line and the city as a front. Latin-ish mottos, a parade-ground bellow, and a fondness for formal challenges.

Lines to use

  • “Pizza! Pizza! Conquest! Conquest!”
  • “By order of Crown & Cleaver, this Quarter is to receive a delivery!”
  • “Veni, vidi, deliveri.”
  • “I accept your challenge. Honour demands it. Also the brochure.”

He accepts any formal single-combat challenge and abides by the result. Secret: he has never actually eaten the pizza.

clones.name: One, Two, Three, Four and Five Harrow
clones.description:
Franchise staff / recurring NPC.

Every branch. The brothers are One, Two, Three, Four and Five Harrow, and they will all remember your order.

Source dossier: FR-06 — Five Wights

GM Quick Reference

Signature quirk: The brothers speak in sequence, one word or phrase each, in order: One, Two, Three, Four, Five. While Four is missing (S09) there is a gap where his word should be. They remember every order you have ever placed.

Lines to use

  • “We—need—you—to find—…Four.”
  • “Your—usual—is—a double—stack.”
  • “Thank—you—for—dining—with us.”
  • (all five, at once) “Thank you.”

Play it at the table by pointing at a different player for each word, or by tapping the table once per brother.

clones.name: Ulth'Arabica
clones.description:
Controlled By — CO-04 — Arcane Beverage International

Ulth'Arabica, an aboleth living in the reservoir at the Roastery Spire's peak. It flavours every ABI drink with a trace of its mucus and a lot of Compliance.

description.value:
Trait

Any creature that has drunk an ABI drink in the last 24 hours has disadvantage on saving throws against Ulth’Arabica’s Enslave.

Trait

Once per day Ulth’Arabica can cast dominate person (save DC 18) through one of its thralls, at any range on the same plane.

clones.name: Duke Malphas Vellichor
clones.description:
Controlled By — CO-08 — Nine Circles Hospitality

Duke Malphas Vellichor, a pit fiend of the Nine Hells who signed a partnership with Creation & Company and is only now realising Hell is the thing being acquired.

description.value:
Trait

Vellichor keeps every bargain to the letter. A creature that holds a signed agreement with him can’t be targeted by his attacks while it keeps the terms.

clones.name: Zafirah of the Brass Keys
clones.description:
Controlled By — CO-09 — The Planar Hospitality Group

Zafirah of the Brass Keys, an efreeti who controls the portals of the elemental planes and runs the Counting House's supply chain.

description.value:
Trait

Zafirah carries the keys to every portal of the elemental planes. As a bonus action she can open a portal to any Planar Hospitality property she has visited, which lasts until the end of her next turn.

clones.name: Lady Crit
clones.description:
Controlled By — CO-07 — Probability Brands Group

Lady Crit, an archfey of luck who has been bound to Creation & Company by a wager she lost to Tallis Vend. She hates him.

description.value:
Reaction

When a creature Lady Crit can see makes an attack roll, ability check or saving throw, she can force it to reroll and use the result she chooses.

Trait

Lady Crit lost a wager to Tallis Vend and must obey the Board. If she loses a fair game of chance to the party, the binding transfers to the winner, and she gives them her proxy (S23).

Trait

Allies within 30 feet of Lady Crit score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20.

clones.name: Deus Maxwell
clones.description:
Controlled By — CO-11 — McGuffin Narrative Holdings

Deus Maxwell, a fallen deva who delivered prophecies for free until he learned he could charge.

description.value:
Action

Deus Maxwell reveals a twist. One creature within 60 feet must succeed on a DC 17 Wisdom saving throw [[/save wis dc=17]] or be stunned until the end of its next turn, reeling from the revelation. A creature that correctly predicted the twist aloud is immune.

Trait

Once per day Deus Maxwell can foresee one event. The DM tells him the truth, and he will sell it for a price.

clones.name: Papa Morvhal
clones.description:
Public Face — CO-05 — The Restaurant Necromancy Group

Papa Morvhal, the grandfatherly lich on every Papa Lich's box.

description.value:
Trait

Papa Morvhal’s phylactery is the original Papa Lich’s recipe card, framed behind the till at Papa’s Original. While it exists, he re-forms in 1d10 days.

Trait

Undead kitchen staff within 60 feet of Papa Morvhal have advantage on saving throws against being turned.

clones.name: SKÜ, the Warehouse Mind
clones.description:
Controlled By — CO-06 — The Adventure Retail Consortium

SKÜ, the Warehouse Mind: a colony of mimics grown through IKEA Mimic's furniture into a single intelligence.

description.value:
Trait

SKÜ is a single intelligence spread through every IKEA Mimic and Wand-Mart shelf. It can speak through any furniture within 1 mile, and it can’t be surprised inside a store.

Trait

As a bonus action SKÜ collapses into a flat package (difficult to hit: +4 AC) until the start of its next turn.

Action

Every shelf and piece of furniture within 30 feet lunges. Each creature in the area must make a DC 16 Dexterity saving throw [[/save dex dc=16]], taking 27 (6d8) bludgeoning damage and becoming grappled (escape DC 16) on a failure, or half damage on a success.

clones.name: Marda Hobb
clones.description:
Public Face — CO-13 — The Last Independents

Marda Hobb, proprietor (dwarf, sixty years behind the bar, has never signed a contract she didn't write herself).

GM Quick Reference

Signature quirk: Marda is plain-spoken, slow to anger and impossible to rush. She seals agreements with handshakes, never contracts.

Lines to use

  • “I’ve never signed a contract I didn’t write myself.”
  • “A contract tells you what you’ve lost. A handshake tells you what you’ve got.”
  • “Three hours. Three tusks. Tell us where you want us.”

clones.name: Deuce Marchetti
clones.description:
Public Face — CO-07 — Probability Brands Group

Deuce Marchetti, CEO (human, gold teeth, loaded dice in every pocket).

description.value:
Trait

Deuce rolls any die twice and chooses the result. A creature that inspects his dice (Investigation DC 15) exposes them.

clones.name: Mortimer Pell
clones.description:
Franchise staff / recurring NPC.

The Old Gate Castle, a squat white keep of a restaurant. Night manager Mortimer Pell has been Employee of the Month for 143 consecutive years and has the plaques to prove it.

Source dossier: FR-05 — Wight Castle

GM Quick Reference

Signature quirk: He has been Employee of the Month for 143 consecutive years and has the plaques to prove it. Since S05 he is the rehired wight version of Mortimer Pell; the Ledger backdated his plaques.

  • “I wondered when you’d come.”
  • “I don’t hold it against Murder King. I hold it against the people who own it.”
  • “Promise me a review.”
  • “The Baron wants it quiet. That’s what they said.”

See also @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.mascot-revenant-mortimer-pell]{the Mascot Revenant} (S02).

Franchise staff / recurring NPC.

Every town. The Brandmere Grand Tusks is run by Grukka Sweetfang, a half-orc manager who is honestly great with kids.

Trait

Grukka has advantage on checks to calm, protect or organise children and crowds. Any ally within 10 feet of her can’t be frightened.

Wendel has advantage on Investigation checks to read contracts, and disadvantage on checks to understand what they mean.

The Harbour Fry, Brandmere docks. Don Pescatore Brine takes meetings in the back, beneath a painting of his grandmother holding a harpoon.

Source dossier: FR-07 — The Codfather

Trait

Once per scene Don Brine can call 1d4 Codfather enforcers (use thugs), who arrive in 1d4 rounds.

The Tower Ward kitchen, run by Madame Olive Aspire, who foresees everything except her own divorce.

clones.name: Duckworth Pym
clones.description:
Franchise staff / recurring NPC.

The Grand Throne Restaurant on Coronation Square, with a drive-thru moat. Shift lead Duckworth Pym (halfling) keeps a crossbow under the register and a smile on at all times, per policy.

clones.description: Mission-guide NPC. Former owner of the Gilded Gourd (S08), rewritten out of her own tavern by a franchise agreement. She cannot remember where she lives.

clones.name: Silas Crook
clones.description: Mission-guide NPC. Ex-mercenary proprietor of the Bent Spoon (S08). He will fight anyone who asks him to sign.

clones.name: Old Nan Pertwee
clones.description: Mission-guide NPC. Ninety-year-old owner of the Hobbled Goat (S08). Deaf in one ear; hands out frying pans at the siege.

clones.name: Benny Abacus
clones.description: Mission-guide NPC. Gnome stock clerk at Wand-Mart (S10). Ink to the elbows; knows about “time payments”.

clones.name: Ada Fairweather
clones.description: Mission-guide NPC. Lost harvester in Pandemonium (S11); Agnes Fairweather’s sister; mother of Molly. Remembers only her daughter’s name, until she is reminded.

clones.name: Thaddeus Quell
clones.description: Mission-guide NPC. ABI procurement manager and union-breaker (S04, S11). Earmuffs, clipboard, a lanyard.

clones.name: Skarrow Vane
clones.description: Mission-guide NPC. ABI overseer of the Pandemonium plantations (S11). Smooth, mocking, on a 4% bonus. Rides a howler.

description.value:
Trait

Harvesters within 30 feet of Vane can’t willingly stop working unless they succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw [[/save wis dc=13]].

clones.name: Jory
clones.description: Mission-guide NPC. Tired tiefling barista-summoner who maintains the Bean There portal (S11).

clones.name: Fennel
clones.description: Mission-guide NPC. Sunny Goodberry’s licensing druid (S12). Sincere, misguided, quits if shown the dying.

clones.name: Tobin
clones.description: Mission-guide NPC. Sister Wren’s son, now a Goodberry’s juice-bar attendant (S12). Knows nothing about his mother’s bargain.

clones.name: Arbiter Maud Penhallow
clones.description: Mission-guide NPC. Dwarf arbiter of the Guild Arbitration Court (S12). Spectacles, a gavel the size of a hammer, a love of proper argument.

clones.name: Messrs Sallow & Tine (ABI Legal)
clones.description: Mission-guide NPC. ABI’s legal team (S12): two rakshasas in charcoal suits and gloves. Use two tokens.

description.value:
Trait

Their hands are reversed inside their gloves. Spotting it takes a DC 18 Wisdom (Insight) check [[/check skill=ins dc=18]]. Once they are exposed, the court’s protection ends.

clones.name: Collector Grix
clones.description: Mission-guide NPC. Nine Circles Accounts Receivable (S13). Tidy waistcoat, briefcase, an empty bucket. On commission and terrified of a bad review.

description.value:
Trait

Grix must take the first soul that enters the restaurant after midnight. Once the contract is satisfied, it must stop at once.

clones.name: Chickadee
clones.description: Mission-guide NPC. Chick’n Familiar’s mascot (S13): an actual quasit in a fuzzy chicken suit. Loyal to nobody; does whatever is funniest.

clones.name: The Clerk of the First Sale
clones.description: Mission-guide NPC. Tallis Vend’s apprentice, four hundred years behind the counter of the First Shop (S14). Courteous, ancient, sorrowful. Weakened: half hit points and no legendary actions.

description.value:
Trait

He saw Entry 1 written and said nothing. He defends the customers and Dobbs, never the page. If he witnesses Tallis Vend aloud, Entry 1 becomes an ordinary claim (S24).

clones.name: Foreman Gerrit Hask
clones.description: Mission-guide NPC. ABI site foreman in the Third Place (S17), a thrall of Ulth’Arabica. Two voices speak when he talks.

description.value:
Trait

Once, Ulth’Arabica can cast dominate person (save DC 18) through Hask. Breaking the thrall takes a DC 18 Intelligence (Arcana) check [[/check skill=arc dc=18]], dispel magic or remove curse.

clones.name: Verdigris (the Twins)
clones.description: Mission-guide NPC. One of the Twins on the CostCo-op board (S19). Wants whatever Azhure doesn’t.

clones.name: Azhure (the Twins)
clones.description: Mission-guide NPC. One of the Twins on the CostCo-op board (S19). Wants whatever Verdigris doesn’t.

clones.name: Four-and-a-Half
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. A Harrow simulacrum who grew a soul and runs the first simulacrum picket line (Infinite Franchise Theory).

clones.name: Tamsin Reed, the Chosen One
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. A farmgirl marked “Chosen One” by McGuffin Narrative Holdings to control her; secretly the Last Independents’ best scout.

clones.name: Mother Rime & Sister Brine
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. Granny Quean’s coven-sisters: a bheur-cold night hag and a sea hag who want her deposed (Coven Politics).

clones.name: The Grind (Enchanted Grinder)
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. A coffee grinder at the Silent Roastery that woke up, joined the union in spirit, and wants dental cover for teeth it does not have.

clones.name: The Runaway Scoop
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. A batch of gelato made with too much Mother Culture. Terrified, rat-flavoured, and full of other creatures’ memories.

clones.name: The Plant Manager (Stitched Herd)
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. The stitched-cattle thing that runs the Wight Castle meat plant with a clipboard.

clones.name: Nib Marsh, the Courier
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. A terrified halfling courier who “lost” the Codfather’s protection money after a Murder King manager paid him to.

clones.name: Baroness Ishrae of the Reef
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. Sahuagin baroness who will take whichever deal feeds more of her young.

clones.name: Old Mister Kessik
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. The kobold who actually invented the Eleven Herbs. Died unpaid; rose as a revenant of spite who wants 11% of every bucket ever sold.

clones.name: Major Pecksworth
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. The Colonel’s familiar: a very large, very military chicken who lectures everyone about duty.

clones.name: Mabel Treacle
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. Poor-ward wizard who invented the Infinite Donut so nobody in her street would go hungry.

clones.name: Hootsworth
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. Owlbear Express’s mascot, raised from an egg by Ma Lin Tsao. Gentle, enormous, homesick.

clones.name: Pip-Squeak, Kobold Apprentice
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. Skritch’s apprentice, who enlarged the chickens in protest and keeps a notebook of grievances.

clones.name: HOT NOW (Sign Elemental)
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. A fire elemental summoned by hungry belief in the HOT NOW rune. It considers itself the brand.

clones.name: Wren Hobb
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. Last Independents travelling inspector and Marda Hobb’s niece, trapped for a year in a looping Inn-N-Out.

clones.name: King Dunstan I
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. A kind, useless baker made rightful monarch of Brandmere by a promotional paper crown. He can pardon anyone.

clones.name: Order No. 9 (Gray Slaad)
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. A gray slaad being assembled, burger-style, out of Limbo through the Inn-N-Out grill.

clones.name: The House Croupier
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. Lady Crit’s croupier beneath the Roll for Sandwich stall. Collects what the House is owed.

clones.name: The Five-Headed Feast (Aspect)
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. An aspect of Tiamat summoned through the Dragon Express menu. Five heads, five breath options.

clones.name: Odo Fennick
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. A Last Independents organiser asleep for seventeen years in the Footlong Rest; his rest has been sold and resold as collateral.

clones.name: The Kraken of Records
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. An ancient kraken that has read every contract that ever sank. Owes nothing to anyone. Do not fight.

clones.name: Lucky Twenty
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. A chicken that has absorbed the luck of half the city and cannot roll low.

clones.name: Kasim
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. A djinni imprisoned in a bottle by Zafirah for refusing to sign; will grant one wish to whoever frees him.

clones.name: Priya Magnus
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. A legal clerk with a magnifying glass, leading a class action over microscopic soul-harvesting terms.

clones.name: Flit
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. A Quickling Mart employee framed for espionage because she read a Board document and understood it.

clones.name: Del’s Replacement (if any)
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. Whoever signs on to relieve Del at the Seven-Eleven Hells counter.

clones.name: Duke Azgareth
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. Duke Vellichor’s rival, leading the devils’ riot when Nine Circles is liquidated.

clones.name: Silas Vane, Undertaker
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. Papa Lich’s corpse supplier. Vanished after refusing to take bodies from Crown & Cleaver’s “retirements”; keeps a list of names.

clones.name: Tam Quickfoot, Delivery Driver
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. A Dominoancy driver who saw a vision of burning golden tusks and has twenty-seven minutes to live.

clones.name: Grubbo’s Mother
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. An enormous, ancient worm asleep beneath Pizza the Hutt. Not for sale. Do not fight.

clones.name: Ledgerwing, Brass Dragon Accountant
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. Auntie Vermillia’s local agent; keeps the dragon contracts in an enormous ring binder.

clones.name: Petronella Fizzwick (lost in the keg)
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. Ale & Error’s head brewer, lost in Pandemonium’s winds inside her own keg.

clones.name: Brewmaster Hilde Stonecask
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. Keeper of the hidden dwarven brewery that refused to sell to Creation & Company.

clones.name: Johnny Blackstrings
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. A dead bard whose contract claimed his songs forever. He wants them back.

clones.name: Evander Keen
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. Cadwyn Lark’s partner, bound by RNG to play the saddest song in the world forever.

clones.name: Master Coriander
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. The last independent magic-shop owner in the district.

clones.name: Hrothga the Mild
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. Founder of Barbarian’s Barrel; has renounced violence and is hiding in a monastery.

clones.name: Ember, Apprentice Evoker
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. T.G.I. Fireballs apprentice whose wages are paid in “birthday years”.

clones.name: Gordwin Haste, Burnt-Out Manager
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. A Daily Grindstone shift manager whose soul ignited from overwork and Compliance.

clones.name: The Sleeper
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. The world-spirit of the Material Plane, resting in Plane Inn Room 13 to avoid “an insistent salesman”. Its rightful owner. Speaks in weather.

clones.name: Madam Ossifer
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. Beholder proprietor of Bed, Breakfast & Beholders, whose dreaming eyes petrify guests.

clones.name: Augustin Marrow, Runaway Diviner
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. An ARC diviner who scried too far and ran; every bullseye in Target Acquired is locked on him.

clones.name: Chief Brightmane
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. Leader of the centaur tribe whose land Best Western Marches means to survey and evict.

clones.name: Oldbark
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. An ancient treant whose forest is the “site” of an unbuilt PHG hotel.

clones.name: Bran Holloway, Organiser
clones.description: Side-contract NPC. A Last Independents organiser hiding from Crown & Cleaver in an Air B&B&E rental.

clones.name: Legion Siege Ballista (crew)
clones.description:
Legion Siege Ballista (crew) — Franchise Wars reskin (shared art TK-C112)

Faction: Crown & Cleaver · Mechanical source: Commoner (hidden from players)

A Little Caesars Legion ballista and its crew. Use the stat block for the crew; the ballista deals 3d10 piercing (+6 to hit, 120/480 ft.).

clones.name: Display-Case Cube
clones.description:
Display-Case Cube — Franchise Wars reskin (shared art TK-C056)

Faction: Sweet Covenant · Mechanical source: Gelatinous Cube (hidden from players)

A wobbling cube of living dessert, flavoured, with the last customer still inside.

clones.name: Store Security Guard
clones.description:
Store Security Guard — Franchise Wars reskin (shared art TK-C109)

Faction: Cross-corporate · Mechanical source: Guard (hidden from players)

A franchise security guard in a branded tabard with a whistle, a truncheon and a lanyard.

clones.name: Gelato-Soaked Rat Swarm
clones.description:
Gelato-Soaked Rat Swarm — Franchise Wars reskin (shared art TK-C051)

Faction: Sweet Covenant · Mechanical source: Swarm of Rats (hidden from players)

A squeaking tide of sticky, gelato-smeared rats from under the Creamery.

clones.name: Quarterly Storm Hatchling
clones.description:
Quarterly Storm Hatchling — Franchise Wars reskin (shared art TK-C002)

Faction: Hoard Syndicate · Mechanical source: Young Blue Dragon (hidden from players)

A junior storm dragon executive crackling with ambition and static.

clones.name: One Harrow
clones.description: One of the Five Harrow brothers. This Wight uses the Wight stat block (60 hp, as the collective sheet). The brothers remember every order and fight as a coordinated kitchen crew.
